ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The sex determination of birds is ZW type. The eye color of a certain bird species is controlled by two independently inherited pairs of genes (A, a and B, b). A and B are two pure-breeding varieties, both with red eyes. According to the following crossing results, infer what the genotypes of the parents A and B in cross I are respectively.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: A is aaZBZB, B is AAZbW

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The sex determination of birds is ZW type. The eye color of a certain bird species is controlled by two independently inherited pairs of genes (A, a and B, b). A and B are two pure-breeding varieties, both with red eyes. According to the following crossing results, infer what the genotypes of the parents A and B in cross I are respectively.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: A is aaZBZB, B is AAZbW
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives two groups of reciprocal crossing results. Cross 1 is “♂ A × B ♀,” and its F1 result is written as “both females and males are brown-eyed.” Cross 2 is “♀ A × B ♂,” and its F1 result is written as “males are brown-eyed, females are red-eyed.” Reasoning: The stem states that birds have ZW type sex determination, that is, males are ZZ and females are ZW; A and B are both pure-breeding red-eyed, and eye color is controlled by two independently inherited genes A/a and B/b. Two red-eyed pure-breeding varieties can produce brown-eyed offspring after crossing, indicating that brown eyes require both dominant genes A and B at the same time, and lacking either dominant gene results in red eyes. Therefore A and B should be complementary at the two pairs of genes. The reciprocal crossing results are different, and in cross 2 only female F1 are red-eyed, indicating that one pair of genes is located on the Z chromosome; the Z chromosome of female birds comes only from the father. Let A/a be an autosomal gene, and B/b be a Z-linked gene. In cross 1, A is male and, to make all offspring have B, should be ZBZB; A itself is red-eyed, so it should lack A, namely aa. B is female and should provide dominant A, so it should be AA; B itself is red-eyed, so on the Z chromosome it is b, namely ZbW. Therefore the parents in cross 1 are: A aaZBZB, B AAZbW. Verification of cross 2: A female aaZBW × B male AAZbZb, F1 males are AaZBZb, having A and B, and are brown-eyed; F1 females are AaZbW, lacking B, and are red-eyed, consistent with the results shown in the figure.
